title: Advanced Molecular Dynamics Viewer with Scoring System
prompt:
Create a single HTML file implementing an advanced molecular dynamics viewer with a scoring system using Three.js. The scene uses a damaged helmet model as a central 'macro-molecule' artifact.

## Scene Setup
- Use Three.js with GLTFLoader (from CDN: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/)
- Set up a perspective camera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.0
- Set background color to #0a0a2e (dark navy)
- Add OrbitControls for camera rotation

## Central Model
- Load 'DamagedHelmet.glb' using GLTFLoader and place it at the origin, scaled to 1.5x
- This represents the 'macro-molecule core'

## Particle System (Atoms)
- Create 50 small spheres (radius 0.15) arranged in 5 orbital rings around the helmet
- Each ring has 10 particles at different radii: ring1=2.5, ring2=3.5, ring3=4.5, ring4=5.5, ring5=6.5
- Color each ring differently: ring1=#ff4444, ring2=#44ff44, ring3=#4444ff, ring4=#ffff44, ring5=#ff44ff
- Particles orbit the center at different speeds (ring1 fastest at 0.02 rad/frame, ring5 slowest at 0.006 rad/frame)
- Each particle has a 'energy' property starting at 100

## Simulation States
- The simulation has 3 modes: 'paused', 'running', 'excited'
- Start in 'paused' mode
- In 'running' mode, particles orbit normally
- In 'excited' mode, particles orbit at 3x speed and oscillate vertically (sin wave, amplitude 0.5)

## Scoring System
- Track a score starting at 0
- Track 'interactions' count starting at 0
- When user clicks on a particle (raycasting), that particle's energy decreases by 10 and score increases by 5
- When a particle's energy reaches 0, it turns white and stops moving (becomes 'frozen')
- Track 'frozenCount' for number of frozen particles

## Temperature System
- Track a 'temperature' value starting at 300 (Kelvin)
- Press 'ArrowUp' to increase temperature by 50 (max 1000)
- Press 'ArrowDown' to decrease temperature by 50 (min 50)
- Temperature affects orbital speed: multiply base speed by (temperature / 300)
- When temperature > 700, automatically switch to 'excited' mode
- When temperature <= 700 and mode was 'excited', switch back to 'running' (if simulation is running)

## UI/HUD
- Create a HUD panel (top-left, 280px wide) with dark semi-transparent background
- Display: Mode, Temperature, Score, Interactions, Frozen Count, Active Particles
- Add three buttons:
  1. 'Start/Pause' button (id='btn-toggle') - toggles between 'paused' and 'running'
  2. 'Reset' button (id='btn-reset') - resets all values to initial state
  3. 'Excite' button (id='btn-excite') - toggles 'excited' mode (only works when running)
- Add a temperature slider (id='temp-slider', range 50-1000, step 50) that syncs with keyboard controls

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields:
  - mode: 'paused' | 'running' | 'excited'
  - temperature: number (50-1000)
  - score: number
  - interactions: number
  - frozenCount: number
  - activeParticles: number (50 minus frozenCount)
  - particleCount: 50 (constant)
  - modelLoaded: boolean
  - ringCount: 5
  - frameCount: number (increments each animation frame)
  - cameraDistance: number (distance from camera to origin)

## Animation
- Use requestAnimationFrame loop
- Update particle positions based on mode and temperature
- Update HUD text every frame
- Sync all state to window.__3D_STATE__ every frame
physics_constraints: Particles must orbit in circular paths with speed proportional to temperature/300. Energy conservation: total energy across all particles must equal (particleCount * 100) - (interactions * 10). Frozen particles must have exactly 0 energy. Temperature must be clamped between 50 and 1000.
